fact: Counting for Cameroon's 4th general population and housing census, launched 24 April 2026 and coupled with the agriculture and livestock census, closed on 15 September 2026 with unofficial, unconsolidated coverage of about 75% (60% at 31 July), below the 90-95% standards.

A Prime Minister's order made public 31 July 2026 set a complementary enumeration period from 1 August to 15 September 2026 for the 4th general population and housing census, to find households not yet identified or counted.

A pilot of the 4th general population and housing census ran October to November 2025 in four localities (Bamenda 1, Fongo Tongo, Buea, Mora) with UNFPA support, and 49 agents and supervisors were trained on digital collection tools.
Recruitment of 32,059 enumerators for the 4th census was under way, with a budget of 13.28 billion FCFA and fieldwork due to start 24 April 2026; the document is dated 11 March 2026.

Order 111/CAB/PM of 30 July 2026 set an additional collection period from 1 August to 15 September 2026 for the joint enumeration of the 4th population and housing census, after orders of 6 March and 29 May 2026 set and extended the dates.

The national statistical information council's session of 7 April 2026 recalled that the 2026 annual budget plan of FCFA 31.5bn (12.8bn domestic, 18.2bn external) funds the main 2026 actions, including the fourth General Population and Housing Census (RGPH); Cameroon Tribune reports this.
